# rich_click

*module*

rich-click is a minimal Python module to combine the efforts of the excellent packages 'rich' and 'click'.

The intention is to provide attractive help output from Click, formatted with Rich, with minimal
customization required.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/__init__.py#L1-L1)

**Modules**

- `rich_click.cli`
- `rich_click.decorators`
- `rich_click.patch`
- `rich_click.rich_async_command`
- `rich_click.rich_box`
- `rich_click.rich_click`
- `rich_click.rich_click_theme`
- `rich_click.rich_command`
- `rich_click.rich_context`
- `rich_click.rich_group`
- `rich_click.rich_help_configuration`
- `rich_click.rich_help_formatter`
- `rich_click.rich_help_rendering`
- `rich_click.rich_panel`
- `rich_click.rich_parameter`
- `rich_click.testing`
- `rich_click.utils`

*module* · *Added in 1.2.0*

The command line interface.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/cli.py#L1-L1)


[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/cli.py#L32-L36)

## rich_click.cli.main

*function* · *Added in 1.2.0*

```python
def main(ctx: RichContext, script_and_args: tuple[str, ...], theme: str, output: Literal[None, 'html', 'svg'], errors_in_output_format: bool, suppress_warnings: bool, patch_rich_click: bool, rich_config: dict[str, Any] | None, show_help: bool) -> None
```

The [link=https://github.com/ewels/rich-click]rich-click[/] CLI provides
[#FF6B6B bold]r[/][#FF8E53 bold]i[/][#FFB347 bold]c[/][#4ECDC4 bold]h[/][#45B7D1 bold]l[/][#74B9FF bold]y[/]
formatted help output from any
tool using [link=https://click.palletsprojects.com/]click[/], formatted with
[link=https://github.com/Textualize/rich]rich[/].

Full docs here: [link=https://ewels.github.io/rich-click/latest/documentation/rich_click_cli/]https://ewels.github.io/rich-click/latest/documentation/rich_click_cli/[/]

The rich-click command line tool can be prepended before any Python package
using native click to provide attractive richified click help output.

For example, if you have a package called [argument]my_package[/] that uses click,
you can run:

>>> [command]rich-click[/] [argument]my_package[/] [option]--help[/]

When not rendering help text, the provided command will run normally,
so it is safe to replace calls to the tool with [command]rich-click[/] in front, e.g.:

>>> [command]rich-click[/] [argument]my_package[/] [argument]cmd[/] [option]--foo[/] 3

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/cli.py#L285-L521)

## rich_click.decorators.argument

*function* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def argument(*param_decls: str, cls: type[click.Argument] | None = None, **attrs: Any) -> Callable[[FC], FC]
```

Add a positional argument to the command.

The same as `click.argument`, but the argument is a `RichArgument` unless you set `cls`.

**Parameters**

- `*param_decls` (`str`) (default: `()`) — Name of the argument.
- `cls` (`type[click.Argument] | None`) (default: `None`) — Argument class. Defaults to `RichArgument`.
- `**attrs` (`Any`) (default: `{}`) — Other arguments for the `cls` constructor, such as `nargs` and `type`. See `click.Argument`.

**Returns**

- (`Callable[[FC], FC]`) — A decorator that adds the argument to a command.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/decorators.py#L347-L364)

Set the help configuration and the Rich console of one command or group.

## rich_click.decorators.version_option

*function* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def version_option(version: str | None = None, *param_decls: str, package_name: str | None = None, prog_name: str | None = None, message: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> Callable[[FC], FC]
```

Add a `--version` option that prints the version and exits.

**Parameters**

- `version` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Version to print. If not set, Click reads it from the metadata of the installed `package_name`. If Click cannot find the version, `--version` raises a `RuntimeError`.
- `*param_decls` (`str`) (default: `()`) — Option names. Defaults to `--version`.
- `package_name` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Installed package to read the version from. If not set, it is the top-level package of the module that calls `version_option`.
- `prog_name` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Name of the CLI in the message. If not set, Click uses the name of the command.
- `message` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Message to print. It can use `%(prog)s`, `%(package)s` and `%(version)s`. Defaults to `"%(prog)s, version %(version)s"`.
- `**kwargs` (`Any`) (default: `{}`) — Other arguments for `option`.

**Returns**

- (`Callable[[FC], FC]`) — A decorator that adds the option to a command.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/decorators.py#L423-L459)

# rich_click.patch

*module* · *Added in 1.8.0*

Patch click, Typer or asyncclick so that their commands print help and errors with rich-click.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/patch.py#L1-L1)

## rich_click.patch.patch

*function* · *Added in 1.8.0*

```python
def patch(rich_config: RichHelpConfiguration | None = None, *, patch_rich_click: bool = True, patch_typer: bool = False, module: Any | None = None) -> None
```

Patch Click internals to use rich-click types.

**Parameters**

- `rich_config` (`RichHelpConfiguration | None`) (default: `None`) — Help configuration to apply globally.
- `patch_rich_click` (`bool`) (default: `True`) — Also patch the `rich_click` namespace. Ignored when `module` is set.
- `patch_typer` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — Also patch Typer. Ignored when `module` is set.
- `module` (`Any | None`) (default: `None`) — An asynchronous click fork, such as `asyncclick`, to patch instead of click. rich-click then installs its async command classes into the namespace of that module. Requires `rich-click[async]`.

**Raises**

- `TypeError` — `module` is not an asynchronous click fork, such as asyncclick.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/patch.py#L340-L415)

## rich_click.patch.patch_typer

*function* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def patch_typer(rich_config: RichHelpConfiguration | None = None) -> None
```

Patch Typer so that its commands print help and errors with rich-click.

**Parameters**

- `rich_config` (`RichHelpConfiguration | None`) (default: `None`) — Help configuration for every command.

> **Warning**
>
> Typer 0.26 and later may not support the patch, so the function always shows a warning on those versions.
> If a Typer class cannot be patched, it shows a second warning and leaves Typer unpatched.
> See [Typer support](https://ewels.github.io/rich-click/latest/documentation/typer_support/#typer-026-support).

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/patch.py#L421-L502)

# rich_click.rich_async_command

*module*

Rich-formatted command classes for asyncclick.

[asyncclick](https://github.com/python-trio/asyncclick) is a fork of click with async command
methods (`main`, `invoke`, `make_context` and `parse_args`). The rich-click mixins
(`RichCommandMixin`, `RichGroupMixin` and `RichContextMixin`) have no click base class, so these
classes combine them with the asyncclick classes.

Most code does not import these classes. Call `rich_click.patch.patch(module=asyncclick)` instead.
It puts these classes into the asyncclick namespace, so `@asyncclick.command` CLIs get rich-click help.

> **Note**
>
> This module needs asyncclick: install `rich-click[async]`. The rest of rich-click never imports it.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_async_command.py#L1-L1)

## rich_click.rich_async_command.RichAsyncCommand

*class*

```python
class RichAsyncCommand(RichCommandMixin, asyncclick.Command)
```

Bases: `rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin`, `asyncclick.Command`

Richly formatted asyncclick Command.

Combines the help and error formatting of `RichCommandMixin` with the
asynchronous `asyncclick.Command` (async `main` and `invoke`).

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_async_command.py#L40-L118)

### rich_click.rich_async_command.RichAsyncCommand.format_help

*method*

```python
def format_help(ctx: click.Context, formatter: click.HelpFormatter) -> None
```

Inherited from: `rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin`

Write the help: the usage, the help text, the options and the epilog.

Each part has its own `format_*` method, so a subclass can override one part.

> **Warning**
>
> After `rich_click.patch.patch()`, rich-click ignores overrides of `format_usage`,
> `format_help_text`, `format_options` and `format_epilog` in subclasses of the patched
> click classes. These overrides expect click's plain help formatter, so rich-click
> writes those parts itself.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_command.py#L178-L196)

### rich_click.rich_async_command.RichAsyncCommand.get_help_option

*method*

```python
def get_help_option(ctx: click.Context) -> click.Option | None
```

Inherited from: `rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin`

## rich_click.rich_async_command.RichAsyncGroup

*class*

```python
class RichAsyncGroup(RichGroupMixin, RichAsyncCommand, asyncclick.Group)
```

Bases: `rich_click.rich_command.RichGroupMixin`, `rich_click.rich_async_command.RichAsyncCommand`, `asyncclick.Group`

Richly formatted asyncclick Group.

Subcommands and subgroups created from this group inherit the async rich classes
via `command_class` and `group_class`, so the whole command tree renders richly.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_async_command.py#L121-L131)

## rich_click.rich_click_theme.RichClickTheme

*class* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
class RichClickTheme
```

A named set of styles for the help output. Select one with `--theme` or the `theme` setting.

Create RichTheme instance.

**Parameters**

- `name` (`str`) — Name of the theme.
- `description` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Description for the theme.
- `hidden` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — If true, hide from rich-click --themes.
- `styles` (`dict[str, Any] | None`) (default: `None`) — Dict of styles that are applied.
- `primary_colors` (`list[StyleType] | None`) (default: `None`) — Description of which colors are applied. Does not do anything, just serves as documentation.
- `post_combine_callback` (`Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any]] | None`) (default: `None`) — After combining two themes, function is called which adjusts the styles.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_click_theme.py#L17-L72)

## rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin

*class*

```python
class RichCommandMixin(_CommandMixinBase)
```

Bases: `_CommandMixinBase`

Mixin providing Rich help-formatting behavior for click Commands.

Contains only formatting/help behavior and Rich-specific instance state, with
no click base of its own, so it can be composed with either `click.Command`
(see `RichCommand`) or a click-compatible fork's Command (e.g.
`asyncclick.Command`) without dragging click's synchronous execution methods
(`main`, `make_context`, `scope`, etc.) into the MRO.

Execution-flow methods (`main` and `to_info_dict`) deliberately live on the
concrete `RichCommand` instead of here, so that async forks can inherit
their own async equivalents. Help and error formatting, including
`get_help_option` and `_error_formatter`, is shared here.

Create Rich Command instance.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_command.py#L53-L260)

### rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin.format_help

*method*

```python
def format_help(ctx: click.Context, formatter: click.HelpFormatter) -> None
```

Write the help: the usage, the help text, the options and the epilog.

Each part has its own `format_*` method, so a subclass can override one part.

> **Warning**
>
> After `rich_click.patch.patch()`, rich-click ignores overrides of `format_usage`,
> `format_help_text`, `format_options` and `format_epilog` in subclasses of the patched
> click classes. These overrides expect click's plain help formatter, so rich-click
> writes those parts itself.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_command.py#L178-L196)

### rich_click.rich_command.RichGroup.context_class

*attribute* · *Added in 1.7.0* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

## rich_click.rich_command.RichGroupMixin

*class*

```python
class RichGroupMixin(RichCommandMixin, _GroupMixinBase)
```

Bases: `rich_click.rich_command.RichCommandMixin`, `_GroupMixinBase`

Mixin providing Rich help-formatting behavior for click Groups.

Like `RichCommandMixin`, this has no click base of its own so it can be
composed with either `click.Group` (see `RichGroup`) or a fork's Group.

Create RichGroup instance.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_command.py#L377-L577)

### rich_click.rich_command.RichGroupMixin.add_command

*method*

```python
def add_command(cmd: click.Command, name: str | None = None, aliases: Iterable[str] | None = None, panel: str | list[str] | None = None) -> None
```

Add a command to this group.

**Parameters**

- `cmd` (`click.Command`) — The command to add.
- `name` (`str | None`) (default: `None`) — Name of the command in this group. Defaults to the name of the command.
- `aliases` (`Iterable[str] | None`) (default: `None`) — Other names that run the command, in addition to the aliases of the command.
- `panel` (`str | list[str] | None`) (default: `None`) — Panel or panels to show the command in, by panel title.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_command.py#L548-L565)

## rich_click.rich_context.RichContextMixin

*class*

```python
class RichContextMixin(_ContextBase)
```

Bases: `_ContextBase`

Rich help formatting for a click Context, as a mixin with no click base class.

`RichContext` combines this mixin with `click.Context`. A click fork combines it
with its own Context class, such as `asyncclick.Context`. Because the mixin has
no click base class, it does not add click's synchronous methods to the fork.

> **Note**
>
> To customize the context of a click CLI, subclass `RichContext`, not this mixin.

Create a context. An argument that is not set takes its value from the parent context.

**Parameters**

- `*args` (`Any`) (default: `()`) — Positional arguments for the click Context.
- `rich_console` (`Console | None`) (default: `None`) — Rich console to print help and errors with.
- `rich_help_config` (`Mapping[str, Any] | RichHelpConfiguration | None`) (default: `None`) — How to format help and errors, as a `RichHelpConfiguration` or a dict of its fields. A dict changes only the fields it names.
- `export_console_as` (`Literal['html', 'svg', 'text'] | None`) (default: `None`) — Export help as `"html"`, `"svg"` or `"text"`, not as terminal output.
- `errors_in_output_format` (`bool | None`) (default: `None`) — Export errors in the `export_console_as` format too.
- `help_to_stderr` (`bool | None`) (default: `None`) — Print help to stderr, not stdout.
- `**kwargs` (`Any`) (default: `{}`) — Keyword arguments for the click Context.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_context.py#L26-L117)


```python
errors_in_output_format: bool = False
```

## rich_click.rich_context.get_current_context

*function* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def get_current_context(silent: bool = False) -> RichContext | None
```

Return the context of the command that runs now.

Use it in helper functions that need the context but do not get it from the `pass_context` decorator.

**Parameters**

- `silent` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — If true, return `None` when no command runs. If false, raise a `RuntimeError`.

**Returns**

- (`RichContext | None`) — The context, or `None` if no command runs and `silent` is true.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_context.py#L138-L150)

```python
def main(args: Sequence[str] | None = None, prog_name: str | None = None, complete_var: str | None = None, standalone_mode: bool = True, windows_expand_args: bool = True, **extra: Any) -> Any
```

## rich_click.rich_help_configuration.RichHelpConfiguration

*class* · *Added in 1.7.0* · *dataclass*

```python
class RichHelpConfiguration
```

Rich Help Configuration class.

When merging multiple RichHelpConfigurations together, user-defined values always
take precedence over the class's defaults. When there are multiple user-defined values
for a given field, the right-most field is used.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_help_configuration.py#L97-L516)

Build a RichHelpConfiguration from globals in rich_click.rich_click.

When building from globals, all fields are treated as having been set by the user,
meaning they will overwrite other fields when "merged".

## rich_click.rich_help_formatter.RichHelpFormatter

*class* · *Added in 1.7.0*

```python
class RichHelpFormatter(click.HelpFormatter)
```

Bases: `click.HelpFormatter`

Rich Help Formatter.

This class is a container for the help configuration and Rich Console that
are used internally by the help and error printing methods.

Create Rich Help Formatter.

**Parameters**

- `indent_increment` (`int`) (default: `2`) — Passed to click.HelpFormatter.
- `width` (`int | None`) (default: `None`) — Passed to click.HelpFormatter. Overrides config.width if not None.
- `max_width` (`int | None`) (default: `None`) — Passed to click.HelpFormatter. Overrides config.max_width if not None.
- `*args` (`Any`) (default: `()`) — Args passed to click.HelpFormatter.
- `console` (`Console | None`) (default: `None`) — Use an external console.
- `config` (`RichHelpConfiguration | None`) (default: `None`) — RichHelpConfiguration. If None, then build config from globals.
- `export_console_as` (`Literal[None, 'html', 'svg', 'text']`) (default: `None`) — How output is rendered by getvalue(). Default of None renders output normally.
- `export_kwargs` (`dict[str, Any] | None`) (default: `None`) — Any kwargs passed to the export method of the Console in getvalue().
- `**kwargs` (`Any`) (default: `{}`) — Kwargs passed to click.HelpFormatter.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_help_formatter.py#L101-L381)

### rich_click.rich_help_formatter.RichHelpFormatter.rich_text

*method* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def rich_text(text: str | Text | Markdown, style: StyleType = '') -> Text | Markdown | RichClickRST
```

Take a string, remove indentations, and return styled text.
By default, return the text as a Rich Text with the request style.

This method uses the config options prefixed `text_` to influence how
rendering works.

**Parameters**

- `text` (`str | Text | Markdown`) — Text to style.
- `style` (`StyleType`) (default: `''`) — Rich style to apply.

**Returns**

- (`Text | Markdown | RichClickRST`) — Text, Markdown, or RichClickRST: Styled text object

## rich_click.rich_help_formatter.create_console

*function* · *Added in 1.7.0*

```python
def create_console(config: RichHelpConfiguration, file: IO[str] | None = None, width: int | None = None, max_width: int | None = None) -> Console
```

Create a Rich console from a help configuration.

**Parameters**

- `config` (`RichHelpConfiguration`) — Help configuration to take the console settings from.
- `file` (`IO[str] | None`) (default: `None`) — Stream to write to. If not set, the console records its output to an in-memory buffer.
- `width` (`int | None`) (default: `None`) — Width of the console. Overrides `config.width`.
- `max_width` (`int | None`) (default: `None`) — Maximum width of the console. Overrides `config.max_width`.

**Returns**

- (`Console`) — The new console.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_help_formatter.py#L52-L98)

```python
class RichClickRichPanel(Panel)
```

*function* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
def get_help_parameter(param: click.Argument | click.Option | RichParameter, ctx: RichContext, formatter: RichHelpFormatter) -> Columns
```

Build primary help text for a click option or argument.
Returns the prose help text for an option or argument, rendered either
as a Rich Text object or as Markdown.
Additional elements are appended to show the default and required status if applicable.

**Parameters**

- `param` (`click.Argument | click.Option | RichParameter`) — Parameter to build help text for.
- `ctx` (`RichContext`) — Click Context object.
- `formatter` (`RichHelpFormatter`) — Formatter object.

**Returns**

- `Columns` (`Columns`) — A columns element with multiple styled objects (help, default, required)

```python
def rich_format_error(formatter: RichHelpFormatter, export_console_as: Literal[None, 'html', 'svg'] = None) -> None
```

Print richly formatted click errors.

Called by custom exception handler to print richly formatted click errors.
Mimics original click.ClickException.echo() function but with rich formatting.

- `formatter` (`RichHelpFormatter`) — formatter object.
- `export_console_as` (`Literal[None, 'html', 'svg']`) (default: `None`) — If set, outputs error message as HTML or SVG.

## rich_click.rich_parameter.RichArgument

*class* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
class RichArgument(RichParameter, click.Argument)
```

Bases: `rich_click.rich_parameter.RichParameter`, `click.Argument`

A positional argument of a command, formatted by rich-click. The `argument` decorator creates one.

Arguments are required by default. With `nargs=-1`, an argument takes any number of values.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/rich_parameter.py#L76-L81)

## rich_click.rich_parameter.RichParameter

*class* · *Added in 1.9.0*

```python
class RichParameter(click.Parameter)
```

Bases: `click.Parameter`

Base class of `RichOption` and `RichArgument`: a click Parameter that rich-click formats in help.

Create RichParameter instance.

# rich_click.testing

*module*

Test helpers for CLIs that use Rich for output and prompts.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/testing.py#L1-L1)

## rich_click.testing.CliRunner

*class*

```python
class CliRunner(click.testing.CliRunner)
```

Bases: `click.testing.CliRunner`

A drop-in replacement for `click.testing.CliRunner` that also isolates Rich.

While a command runs:

- Rich prompts (`rich.prompt.Prompt`, `rich.prompt.Confirm`, and `Console.input()`)
  read from the runner's `input`, including password prompts, which would otherwise call
  `getpass.getpass` and read from the terminal.
- Rich's global console (used by `rich.print()` and prompts without an explicit console) is
  reset in place to follow the runner's `color` setting, and is not interactive.
- Environment variables that change Rich output (`FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`, `COLUMNS`, ...)
  are unset or pinned, unless given in `env`.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/testing.py#L33-L113)

### rich_click.testing.CliRunner.isolation

*method*

```python
def isolation(input: str | bytes | IO[Any] | None = None, env: Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None, color: bool = False) -> Iterator[Any]
```

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/testing.py#L48-L113)

## rich_click.utils.method_is_from_subclass_of

*function* · *Added in 1.8.0*

```python
def method_is_from_subclass_of(base_cls: type[object], method_name: str) -> bool
```

Check to see whether a class's method comes from a subclass of some base class.

This is used under the hood to see whether we would expect a patched RichCommand's help text
methods to be compatible or incompatible with rich-click or not.

[View source](https://github.com/ewels/rich-click/blob/022f47e9f25a36a3d4301fed1e2272df54ed4688/src/rich_click/utils.py#L54-L64)
